definitions.explanation: Paper treated with oil to make it water-resistant. Traditionally used to wrap goods, line umbrellas and raincoats, and keep out moisture before plastics became common.

examples.japanese: {油紙|あぶらがみ}で{包|つつ}む。
{昔|むかし}の{傘|かさ}は{油紙|あぶらがみ}で{作|つく}られていた。
examples.english: Umbrellas in the old days were made from oilpaper.

examples.japanese: {大切|たいせつ}な{書類|しょるい}を{油紙|あぶらがみ}に{包|つつ}んで{湿気|しっけ}から{守|まも}った。
examples.english: I wrapped the important documents in oilpaper to protect them from moisture.

notes:
Paper soaked or coated with drying oil so that it repels water. Once everywhere in daily life—on {番傘|ばんがさ} (traditional umbrellas), raincoats, and packaging—it is now largely replaced by plastic and vinyl.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {油紙|あぶらがみ}で{包|つつ}む: to wrap in oilpaper
- {油紙|あぶらがみ}に{火|ひ}がつく: oilpaper catches fire — also an idiom for someone who talks on and on once they get started

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {蝋紙|ろうがみ}: waxed paper — coated with wax rather than oil
- ビニール: vinyl — the modern waterproof material that replaced oilpaper
